newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan money rates dip, seen up on bond auction.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan money rates dip, seen up on bond auction.

text.p: Pakistan's overnight money rates closed lower on Monday amid excess liquidity but dealers said an auction of six-month federal bonds that attracted 18.6 billion rupees could push rates up soon.

Overnight trading began at five percent but had fallen to two percent by the close, a dealer at KASB & Co said. Lower overnight rates gave borrowers a chance to take one-week funds at 11 percent. One-month borrowers wanted funds at 13 percent but lenders held back expecting the auction to push rates up.
The central bank attracted a total of 18.6 billion rupees in the bond auction with bids in the 16.50/17.4995 percent range.
